items.title: Biotech Deal Week: Lilly, Novo And Novartis Pay Up For Platforms, Not Pipelines
items.summary: Big pharma is still paying up, but more often for delivery and discovery engines than for a single late-stage asset.

items.title: AbbVie vs. Johnson & Johnson: Which Healthcare Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: AbbVie bets on pipeline diversification amid patent cliffs, while J&J's higher profitability masks litigation risks, a choice between growth ambition and defensive stability.

items.title: AbbVie vs. Pfizer: Which Healthcare Stock Makes Your Portfolio Healthier in 2026?
items.summary: AbbVie pivots toward newer immunology drugs while Pfizer leans on acquisitions to offset pandemic decline, but their financial profiles and valuations tell starkly different stories.

items.title: Is LLY Stock Cheaper Than It Looks?
items.summary: At about $1,182 a share, Eli Lilly (LLY) stock trades at about 33.1 times trailing earnings. Those are adjusted earnings: normalized net income with stock-based compensation added back, a basis built to sit close to the one analysts use in their forecasts. That looks expensive. Whether it is depends on two obesity drugs, on margins and on how much Lilly spends buying new medicines.

items.title: Pfizer Stock Paid Out $49B: So Why Did Investors Lose Money?
items.summary: The pharmaceutical giant sent shareholders a torrent of cash, yet the stock itself went backward. Here is the accounting of what owners actually received.

items.title: ABBV vs. JNJ: One of These Dividend Aristocrats Will Crush the Other Over the Next Decade
items.summary: AbbVie and Johnson and Johnson both trade near 52-week highs and carry decades of dividend raises, but one faces a patent cliff and a leveraged balance sheet that could force retirees to rethink their income strategy completely.

items.title: ADARx Pharmaceuticals raises $446 million in upsized IPO
items.summary: The San Diego RNA drug developer sold 26.3 million shares at $17 apiece, with AbbVie investing up to $100 million in a concurrent private placement

items.title: The Peptide Boom That Isn’t About Your Muscles
items.summary: Peptides are everywhere lately.  Influencers inject them for muscle and recovery, and the Food and Drug Administration could soon allow these products to be sold by compounding pharmacies.  While the marketing of these injections to biohackers and wellness consumers will keep generating debate, the peptide boom that matters to biotech investors belongs to a company most TikTokers have never heard of.
